basis: Neurologic injury is common in predominant GA I and severe GA II, supporting an overall rate above ~30%; GA III is usually benign and muscle involvement varies.

decisions.neurologic: involved: striatal injury or metabolic encephalopathy is common across the major symptomatic forms, exceeding approximately 30%; subtype variability limits certainty.

basis: Progressive autoimmune CNS demyelination; optic neuritis is separately diagnosed, and additional direct ocular damage affecting >=30% of this subgroup is not established.

decisions.ocular: none: optic neuritis is a separately diagnosed manifestation; visual symptoms alone do not establish additional ocular damage meeting the threshold in progressive MS.

basis: Inherited vascular malformations; portal hypertension with elevated hepatic transaminases in 1/3 supports functional hepatic involvement, although the sample is small.

decisions.hepatic: involved: portal hypertension with elevated hepatic transaminases in 1/3 patients (~33%) supports clinically consequential hepatic vascular involvement.

basis: Glomus tumor variant usually arising in dermis or subcutis; perivascular differentiation does not itself establish disease of blood vessels.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: origin from modified perivascular smooth-muscle cells does not make this soft-tissue neoplasm a disease occupying or damaging the cardiovascular system.

basis: Myocardial dysfunction and hypoxic brain injury define the syndrome; direct renal ischemia-reperfusion injury occurs in roughly 30-50%.

decisions.renal: involved: ischemia-reperfusion directly injures kidneys in roughly 30-50% after arrest, as part of the syndrome's systemic ischemic injury.

basis: Serine transport disorder with defining neurodevelopmental injury; ankle contracture in 1/2 is secondary to spasticity and does not establish direct musculoskeletal disease.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: ankle contracture is reported in 1/2, but reflects secondary mechanical consequences of neurologic spasticity rather than direct musculoskeletal injury.

basis: Axonal and demyelinating peripheral neuropathy; weakness in ~60-67%, neurogenic muscle changes and foot deformity follow denervation rather than direct muscle or bone disease.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: common weakness and neurogenic atrophy arise from peripheral nerve damage; the muscle findings and secondary foot deformities do not establish direct musculoskeletal disease.

basis: Mandibulofacial dysostosis and bilateral ptosis define the syndrome; external-ear/canal malformations with conductive hearing impairment are major syndromic features; frequency unspecified.

decisions.otologic: involved: congenital external-ear/canal malformations and conductive hearing impairment are major features of the reported syndrome; numerical frequency is unavailable.

basis: Microcephaly and axonal polyneuropathy define the syndrome; characteristic wasting follows denervation, and scoliosis is secondary rather than direct musculoskeletal disease.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: muscle wasting and scoliosis are characteristic but follow neuropathic denervation and weakness; their frequency does not establish direct musculoskeletal injury.

basis: Epileptic neurodevelopmental disorder; conductive hearing impairment in 1/3 (~33%) supports otologic involvement. Cerebral visual impairment and ocular motor signs do not establish eye damage.

decisions.ocular: none: cerebral visual impairment is neurologic; strabismus in 3/6 and nystagmus in 2/6 do not establish direct damage to ocular tissues or the optic nerve.
